Prambanan is a ninth century Hindu temple compound in central Java, the largest in Indonesia. It is dedicated to the three great gods: Shiva, Vishnu and Brahma. Its central Shiva temple rises about 47 metres.

It was built from about 850 under the Sanjaya kings of Mataram, possibly by Rakai Pikatan, and an inscription of 856 seems to record its dedication. It stands only some 50 km from the Buddhist Borobudur, built a generation earlier by the rival Sailendra line, and its tall pointed towers were perhaps a Hindu answer to it. Hundreds of small shrines once surrounded the main temples.

Reliefs on the balustrades tell the Ramayana, the same story told in Old Javanese verse in the Kakawin Ramayana. A Javanese legend links the main statue of Durga to a princess, Rara Jonggrang, turned to stone. The site was abandoned after the court moved east, damaged by earthquakes, and rebuilt in the twentieth century. The 2006 Yogyakarta earthquake damaged it again.
sum: Prambanan is a ninth century Hindu temple compound in central Java, the largest in Indonesia. It is dedicated to the three great gods: Shiva, Vishnu and Brahma. Its central Shiva temple rises about 47 metres.
